subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what trigger plus local editor/tempfile safety contract should it use?
rationale: The implementation path is clear, but launching an environment-selected local editor and writing draft prompts to disk is both a product UX choice and a security boundary that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
options.body: Implement a core TUI composer handoff with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor resolution, restrictive temp draft handling, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold For UX/Security Choice
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers choose the trigger and specify the local editor process and temp-file safety contract.

options.title: Decline External Process Handoff
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers prefer inline multiline editing, composer expansion, or another in-product editor instead of launching local editors.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
recommendation.body: Implement a core TUI composer handoff with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor resolution, restrictive temp draft handling, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this issue and has the strongest recent history across the TUI command and composer lifecycle files.
